Generation and Use of Thermal Energy in the U.S. Industrial Sector and Opportunities to Reduce its Carbon Emissions. NREL/TP-6A50-66763; INL/EXT-16-39680, Revision 1, November 2016. National Renewable Energy Laboratory and Idaho National Laboratory.

Small targeted extraction: the report is a sector energy/emissions analysis with no technology costs or efficiencies for industrial heat sources. Loaded (main): Table 13 heat generators (SIPH/CSP, geothermal, SMR) - assumed unit heat output (MWt) and available temperature (SMR 300-850 degC, geothermal up to 150 degC, SIPH assumed limit 1,000 degC); Table 10 international SMR designs - reactor size (MWt) and reactor outlet temperature for 22 designs by coolant (reprinted from Ingersoll 2015); Sect. 4.1.1 SIPH examples 100 kW-100 MWt at 150-300 degC (reprinted from Rawlins and Ashcroft 2013). Other-values: potential heat supply estimates, Table 14 SMR counts per industry (partial), geothermal resource temperature classes, H2 sizing factors. Not loaded: GHGRP-based sector emissions and energy tables (Tables 1-8), CSP electricity project list (Table 9), geothermal capacity and resource tables (11-12), heat-transfer fluid properties (Table 15). Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 20). No prices or heating values involved. Traps: Table 10 labels HTR-PM as India (it is Chinese) and prints EM2 as "EM" with a footnote marker; Table 13 SIPH temperature is an assumption ("not determined in this study"); SMR temperatures are reactor outlet, not delivered heat; Table 13 title says "Summary of Heat Generators" but the list of tables skips Tables 11-12.
